english: Let $P_{0}$ and $P_{1}$ be the points representing the complex numbers $0$ and $4$ in the Argand plane. For each integer $n\geq0$, let $P_{n+2}$ be the point such that the triangle $P_{n}P_{n+1}P_{n+2}$ is isosceles with the right angle at $P_{n+2}$, and $P_{n+2}$ lies to the right of the directed line from $P_{n}$ to $P_{n+1}$. As $n\to\infty$, the points $P_{n}$ approach the point representing $\alpha+i\beta$, where $\alpha,\beta$ are real and $i=\sqrt{-1}$. Then the value of $\alpha\beta$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $P_{0}$ तथा $P_{1}$ आर्गण्ड तल में सम्मिश्र संख्याओं $0$ तथा $4$ को निरूपित करने वाले बिन्दु हैं। प्रत्येक पूर्णांक $n\geq0$ के लिए माना कि $P_{n+2}$ वह बिन्दु है जिसके लिए त्रिभुज $P_{n}P_{n+1}P_{n+2}$ समद्विबाहु है तथा उसका समकोण $P_{n+2}$ पर है, और $P_{n+2}$, $P_{n}$ से $P_{n+1}$ की ओर निर्दिष्ट रेखा के दाईं ओर स्थित है। जब $n\to\infty$, तब बिन्दु $P_{n}$ उस बिन्दु की ओर अग्रसर होते हैं जो $\alpha+i\beta$ को निरूपित करता है, जहाँ $\alpha,\beta$ वास्तविक हैं तथा $i=\sqrt{-1}$ है। तब $\alpha\beta$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Rotation: $P_{n+2}-P_{n}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}e^{-i\pi/4}(P_{n+1}-P_{n})$ (right side, so clockwise), i.e. $p_{n+2}=c\,p_{n}+(1-c)p_{n+1}$ with $1-c=\dfrac{1-i}{2}$, $c=\dfrac{1+i}{2}$
The other root of $\lambda^{2}-(1-c)\lambda-c=0$ is $-c$, $|c|=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}<1$, so $p_{n}$ converges; the limit $L$ satisfies $L(1+c)=4$
solution_full: Let $p_{n}$ be the complex number of $P_{n}$. In a right isosceles triangle with the right angle at $P_{n+2}$, the side $P_{n}P_{n+2}$ has length $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}P_{n}P_{n+1}$ and makes an angle $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ with $P_{n}P_{n+1}$.

Since $P_{n+2}$ is to the right of the directed line $P_{n}\to P_{n+1}$, the turn from $\overrightarrow{P_{n}P_{n+1}}$ to $\overrightarrow{P_{n}P_{n+2}}$ is clockwise: $p_{n+2}-p_{n}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}e^{-i\pi/4}(p_{n+1}-p_{n})=\dfrac{1-i}{2}(p_{n+1}-p_{n})$.
Check for $n=0$: $p_{2}=\dfrac{1-i}{2}\cdot4=2-2i$, below the real axis (to the right of $0\to4$), and $|p_{2}-0|=|p_{2}-4|=2\sqrt{2}$, $(p_{2}-0)\perp(p_{2}-4)$.
Then $p_{n+2}+c\,p_{n+1}=c\,p_{n}+(1-c)p_{n+1}+c\,p_{n+1}=p_{n+1}+c\,p_{n}$. Hence $p_{n+1}+c\,p_{n}$ is the same for all $n$, equal to $p_{1}+c\,p_{0}=4$.
Convergence: the characteristic equation $\lambda^{2}-(1-c)\lambda-c=0$ has roots $1$ and $-c$, with $|-c|=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}<1$; so $p_{n}=A+B(-c)^{n}\to A$.
Numerical check: $p_{3}=2$, $p_{4}=3-i$, $p_{5}=2-i$, $p_{6}=2.5-0.5i$, and the points spiral in to $2.4-0.8i$.
originality_note: New: an iterated right-isosceles construction gives the complex recurrence p_{n+2} = c p_n + (1-c) p_{n+1}, whose weighted invariant p_{n+1} + c p_n gives the limit point (way 1, iteration). Closest known: the real recurrence x_{n+2} = (x_n + x_{n+1})/2 with limit (x0 + 2x1)/3; the web shows only papers on limit points of other triangle constructions. Different because: the weights are complex (a rotation), so the limit is off the starting line and its position needs the rotation form.

concept_use.Rotation in complex plane: p_{n+2} - p_n = (1/sqrt2) e^{-i pi/4}(p_{n+1} - p_n) encodes the right isosceles triangle on the right side.
concept_use.Geometrical interpretation of complex nu: Right of the directed line means a clockwise turn; the limit point is read as the invariant weighted combination of consecutive points.

key_step: Write the construction as a clockwise rotation-scaling, get the recurrence and its invariant p_{n+1} + c p_n, then the limit.
justification: Rotation set-up plus the invariant of a two-term recurrence with complex weights; the second idea is uncommon in complex numbers but known from real averaging sequences. Placed at 3 (could be read as 4); near 2025-P1-Q9 (L4) for the vector-ratio reasoning but shorter.
